scope: Latest playback intent wins in Pinia and native source publication; heavy preparation is serial and does not own the mixer lock.

nativeBefore.note: Red run after extracting source publication into install, before adding request guards. The source attachment behavior was unchanged at that point.

nativeCoverage: stop/newer request rejects prepared stale source before mixer attachment
editor and preview share request ordering
latest load failure stops the prior source; stale failure leaves newer source alone
thread/channel-controlled old worker cannot attach after stop
queued superseded preparation fails before opening its path
successful output switch invalidates pending playback; failed switch preserves it
real generated WAV: decode, stretch/transpose and positive seek on manually driven mixer
existing pause/resume, immutable buffer and loop resize behavior preserved

bounds.requestBookkeeping: constant-size native generation counter; no per-track history

passed: stale pause error preserves new track
stale resume error preserves new track
stale seek error preserves new track
old tempo response cannot replace new adjustment
seek during preparation starts the requested point with current sync
pause cancels pending resync and keeps its exact source position
resume re-renders canceled sync at the paused position
pending editor play issues native stop
failed restart clears stale playing state
source unmount without closing native session
prepare then explicitly accept without decoding
occupied UI rejects a second offer
duplicate token does not cancel its pending transfer
committed reload recovers from an unconsumed URL token
unowned source is never discarded or decoded
late success cannot clear reset loading
stale error cannot restore previous track
newer opening remains loading until its own response
pinned row pause and hidden stems

limits: Tests use generated WAV files, a software-driven rodio mixer and browser fake IPC; no system audio device or user library is used.
An already running decode or stretch call may finish; cancellation prevents publication and skips superseded waiters but is not a forced DSP interrupt.
Stop and output changes do not wait for the heavy preparation slot; short source installation/seek still uses the mixer and publication locks.
No wall-clock latency, FPS or RSS improvement is claimed.
Cross-platform native device smoke tests were not run.
